hook_text: One to fifty thousand or one to two hundred and fifty thousand. Which map is bigger scale? Most people get it backwards.
clip_script: Two maps. One says 1 to 50 000. The other says 1 to 250 000. Which is the larger scale? Your brain says the big number. Your brain is wrong. A ratio scale is a fraction. One fifty-thousandth of the real size is a bigger slice than one two-hundred-and-fifty-thousandth, just like a fifth of a pizza beats a twenty-fifth. Here is the quick test. There are one hundred thousand centimetres in a kilometre, a one and five zeros. Knock five zeros off. 1 to 50 000: one centimetre is half a kilometre. 1 to 250 000: one centimetre is two and a half kilometres. The first map draws the same road five times longer, with five times the room for detail. Small number after the one, large scale. Big number, small scale. Zoom in, zoom out.
visual_style: Two whiteboard maps side by side with their ratio scales; five zeros fall off each denominator; the same 10 km road is drawn 20 cm long on one and 4 cm long on the other.
mood: Gotcha, then a clean click of understanding.
pacing: Pose the trap, a beat of suspense, then the five-zeros reveal and the side-by-side road.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and convert any scale in three lines.
